{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.",
    "If model shows steady upward trend with no spike, but true outcome has sharp upward spike, model is lagging — adjust forecast to anticipate early breakout.",
    "After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often overcorrects or fails to sustain — reduce forecast slope slightly to avoid overshoot.",
    "When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1), model tends to overestimate — cap forecast growth to avoid overbought bias.",
    "Model consistently underestimates true values in early part of 30d horizon — apply a small upward bias (e.g. +0.5–1.5) to first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.",
    "If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g. after spike), model often holds too high — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.",
    "Sentiment history with multiple 0.2 values suggests market is trending — model should not be flat — apply upward drift correction if no recent spike."
  ]
}
